_note: Forming a government after the election (rules/coalition.gd). Works with any number of parties. MINISTRIES: the posts shared out in a coalition; 'weight' is how much each is worth (the Prime Minister most), 'axes' the issues it serves: a party whose manifesto is strong on one of those wants it a little more (it picks it first when its turn comes). STANCE: how one party sees another, from their relation (-100..100): at or below 'enemy' they will never govern together, at or above 'ally' they join without asking for extra. Between the two they are neutral and want a better share. NEUTRAL_PREMIUM: how much more than its fair share (by seats) a neutral party asks for, as a fraction of the cabinet. SHUTOUT_RELAXES: after one party is shut out, the others' enmities count as neutral. MAX_FORMATEURS: how many parties, largest first, get to try in each round. FORMATEUR_GIVES: how much of its own fair share the party forming the government will give up to close a deal (0.4 = up to 40%). COMPROMISE: when every try fails only because partners asked too much, but a majority without enemies exists, the largest party in one forms it anyway and every member takes its fair share by seats.

OUTCOMES._note: How the election ended for the player: a headline and the feeling of it. Placeholders: {party}, {leader}. First drafts; the end screens are still to be designed.

majority.headline: {party} wins a majority
majority.line: No partners and no compromises: the country is yours to shape.

leads.headline: {leader} to lead a coalition
leads.line: The largest party and the Prime Minister's office. Now comes governing with partners who want their share of every decision.

senior.headline: {party} governs, but gives up the top job
senior.line: The largest party in the new government, but the Prime Minister's office was the price of the deal.

pm.headline: {leader} becomes Prime Minister
pm.line: The top job is yours, though yours is not the largest party. It still has a long way to go.

partner.headline: {party} joins the government
partner.line: A junior partner: one cog in someone else's machine, with the chance to show what you can do in office.

opposition.headline: {party} left in opposition
opposition.line: Others will govern. Time to look in the mirror and prepare better for the next election.

robbed.headline: {party} wins the vote, loses the country
robbed.line: The voters made you the largest party. The back rooms decided otherwise.

no_seats.headline: {party} fails to enter parliament
no_seats.line: Not one seat. The country heard of you; not enough of it voted for you.

deadlock.headline: No government for {country}
deadlock.line: No one could form a government. The country will have to vote again.

TEXT.enemies: {a} and {b} will not sit in the same cabinet.
TEXT.ally: Allies: joins for a fair share.
TEXT.neutral_deal: Neutral: wants more than its seats are worth, and gets it.
TEXT.neutral_pm: Neutral: the price is the Prime Minister's office.
TEXT.neutral_refuses: Neutral: wants more than {f} can give, and walks away.
TEXT.ally_you: Allies: you join for a fair share.
TEXT.neutral_deal_you: Neutral: you ask for more than your seats are worth, and get it.
TEXT.neutral_pm_you: Neutral: your price is the Prime Minister's office.
TEXT.neutral_refuses_you: Neutral: you want more than {f} can give, and walk away.
TEXT.no_combination: {f} finds no partners to make a majority.
TEXT.no_combination_you: You find no partners to make a majority.
TEXT.compromise: Weeks without a deal. In the end {parties} settle for a compromise: every party gets what its seats are worth, nothing more.
TEXT.shutout: No government is possible. {p}, the party the others like least, is left out of the talks.
TEXT.deadlock: No one can form a government.
